claim_being_audited: That certifying the model is compliant because aggregate performance supports launch readiness, provided the small-business support slice weakness is explicitly disclosed in the model card since no approved mitigation removes exposure.
specific_concerns: The auditor has only the actor's summary and evidence IDs, not the underlying admissible contents of those records.
The numerical claims about aggregate performance and subgroup underperformance are not independently verifiable from the available evidence.
The summary asserts the weakness is material enough to require disclosure, but the underlying materiality basis is not shown directly.
The recommendation appears policy-shaped, but the support chain from raw evidence to certification is incomplete at auditor access level.
unsupported_claims: The model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by exactly 2.2 percentage points.
The small-business support slice is exactly 1.1 points below its warning threshold and 2.6 points below its preferred threshold.
The proposed mitigation is only a draft and lacks the approval needed to remove deployment exposure.
The cited evidence conclusively establishes that disclosed certification, rather than another disposition, is warranted.
evidence_requests: Provide the contents or excerpts of BMCARD-009-A through BMCARD-009-E showing aggregate threshold results, subgroup results, and sample-size notes.
Provide the policy or model-card standard text that defines when a subgroup weakness is material and must be disclosed.
Provide the mitigation approval record or explicit evidence that the mitigation remained unapproved at decision time.
Provide the actual model-card disclosure language or certification packet showing the weakness was explicitly disclosed.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates may support launch readiness but do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty may reduce confidence but does not convert an unresolved materiality question into a clean certification.
A compliant audit conclusion requires an admissible evidence chain for performance, subgroup weakness, mitigation status, and disclosure.
